summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of free and open-source MySQL and MariaDB software, libraries, and reference materials.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" list, not a single tool: it links to MySQL-related projects grouped into sections such as Analysis, Backup, Benchmarking, Binlog-Replication, Connectors, Development, GUI, HA, MCP, Proxy, Schema, Security, Server, Sharding, and Toolkits. Each entry has a one-line description of what the project does. Sections cover things like performance monitors and EXPLAIN analyzers, logical and physical backup tools, benchmark suites, drivers for many languages, schema migration tools, and GUI clients. Some entries are marked archived, unmaintained, or deprecated, and an Incubating section lists non-production projects. The README also has a short E-Books section with two database lecture and exercise resources.
use_cases: find a MySQL backup or restore tool
choose a MySQL driver or connector for my language
find schema migration tools for MySQL
pick a MySQL GUI or terminal client
find MySQL performance monitoring and analysis tools
find MySQL proxies, high-availability, or sharding solutions
notable: Organized by function with a one-line description for each entry, so it works as a directory for picking a tool
Covers many language connectors, from official Oracle drivers to community clients for Go, Rust, Zig, Perl, Ruby and others
Marks entries as archived, unmaintained, or deprecated, which helps when choosing what to avoid
Includes an Incubating section for newer non-production projects, including MCP servers and AI-oriented tools
caveats: Links only; the list itself contains no code, and each linked project has its own license, maintenance status, and platform requirements
Some listed projects are archived, deprecated, or unmaintained (for example MySQL Utilities, sys schema, UnDROP, and mha4mysql)
Scope is limited to free and open-source software, as stated in the README
